summary: Reviewed 4 source files (get-queue.ts, resolve-progress.ts, orchestrator-manager.ts, validate-entry.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium finding (path traversal defense-in-depth gap on expectedRepo — noted, does not block). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM — A01 (Broken Access Control / Path Traversal): mcp-server/src/gui/queue/get-queue.ts line 112. In getProjectLedgerStatus(), the `expectedRepo` parameter is used as a path component in `join(ledgerRoot, expectedRepo, slug, 'project-ledger.json')` without content validation. Node.js path.join() does not prevent traversal when a path component contains '../' (e.g., expectedRepo='../secret' would resolve to `<ledgerRoot>/../secret/<slug>/project-ledger.json`). The isRawQueueEntry() guard in validate-entry.ts (line 69) normalizes expectedRepo to `string | null` but only checks `typeof === 'string'` — no pattern/content guard is applied. The SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`) and assertSafeSegment() are already available in src/utils/path-validator.ts and src/utils/constants.ts respectively. Severity context: this is a local developer MCP server with no remote attack surface; the input originates from the Python orchestrator (trusted local process); the operation is read-only and fail-safe. Exploitation would require a malicious `.run-queue.json` on the local filesystem. Practical risk is low, but the fix is trivial and aligns with existing project conventions. Remediation: add a guard in getProjectLedgerStatus() (or at the call sites in getQueue/killQueueEntry/dismissQueueEntry) that rejects non-null expectedRepo values failing assertSafeSegment(). Example: `if (expectedRepo && !assertSafeSegment(expectedRepo)) { return { exists: false, synthesisGenerated: false }; }`

INFO — A01 (Path Traversal, same vector): The `slug` field (expectedSlug in RawQueueEntry) is used as another path component in both the flat and namespaced join() calls. isRawQueueEntry() validates it as a non-empty, non-whitespace-only string but does not apply SAFE_SLUG_REGEX content validation. This is a secondary version of the same defense-in-depth gap — same low exploitability, same trivial fix. The Python orchestrator generates slugs from plan folder basenames (YYYY-MM-DD-{project-name} pattern), so traversal sequences are practically excluded. Remediation: extend assertSafeSegment() coverage to include expectedSlug at the validator boundary (validate-entry.ts).

INFO — A09 (Security Logging): No security-sensitive events (e.g., path traversal attempts, unexpected expectedRepo formats) are logged or surfaced. Since the functions are fail-safe and return `{ exists: false }` on any error, a traversal attempt would silently fall through. A debug-level log on unexpected input format would aid incident detection. Low priority for a local-only tool.

No findings in remaining OWASP Top 10 categories: A02 (no cryptographic operations), A03 (no injection — path.join() used for filesystem access only, no SQL/template/command injection surface), A04 (fail-safe defaults throughout), A05 (no exposed error details — all errors silently return safe defaults), A06 (no new third-party dependencies introduced by WP-007), A07 (no authentication flows), A08 (no deserialization beyond JSON.parse with safe error handling), A10 (no outbound HTTP requests from the modified code paths).
